summary: Jeanne Bliss argues that real, customer-centered operation starts by prioritizing people over accounts and choosing to manage life rather than spread sheets, and by visibly embedding values into how the business runs. She frames a three-action approach to being real, then expands with practical methods: (1) put humanity on the line in how you do business; (2) remove jargon from communications with customers; and (3) surface language issues through an acronym-focused team exercise. The talk also emphasizes walking in customers’ shoes by mapping and stepping through the processes customers experience, and it advocates onboarding that mirrors the customer-centric USAA training approach to instill customer experience into new hires. The examples include airline jargon to illustrate how acronyms can erase human connection, and she invites teams to test their own language and processes against the customer’s perspective.
title: Being Real in Customer Operations: Three Actions to Put Humanity into How You Operate
topics: team activity: stand up, pair off, three-minute acronym talk
airline jargon example (PAX, C-12) as illustration
become a customer: walking in customers' shoes
